narrative:
The model determined that you have a 74.5% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is well above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors, ranked by importance. Your first-year and third-year class rankings had the strongest influence. Being in the bottom decile for both Year 1 and Year 3 grades pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. These rankings are far below the average of accepted students, who typically place around the middle of their class. Your part-time enrollment status was the third most important factor and also increased the likelihood of failure, as nearly 93% of accepted students plan to attend full-time.

Your LSAT score of 31 and undergraduate GPA of 2.70 further reinforced this outlook, both sitting noticeably below the averages of 37.18 and 3.23 seen among accepted applicants. Family income and demographics were not major drivers.

To improve your chances, focus on raising your academic performance to reach at least the middle of your class, consider switching to full-time study if possible, and retake the LSAT aiming for a higher score. These changes would directly address the factors that most hurt your current prediction. (218 words)
